explanations: It is a sturdy cotton, warp-faced textile in which the weft passes under two or more warp threads.
The twill weave produces a diagonal ribbing, which distinguishes it from cotton duck.
The cloth as it is recognised today was first produced in Nîmes, in France.
In the common indigo form only the warp threads are dyed and the weft is left white, so the inside of a pair of jeans is pale.
It is the sturdy cotton cloth used to make jeans and a wide variety of other garments and accessories.

sources.excerpt: Denim is a sturdy, cotton, warp-faced textile in which the weft passes under two or more warp threads.
This twill weave produces a diagonal ribbing that distinguishes it from cotton duck.
Denim, as it is recognised today, was first produced in Nîmes, France.
Denim is available in a range of colors, but the most common type of denim is indigo denim in which the warp threads are dyed while the weft threads are left white.
Jeans made from this cloth are thus predominantly white on the inside.
Denim is used to create a wide variety of garments, accessories, and furniture.
